title.narrative: Lusaka Transmission and Distribution Rehabilitation Project

description.narrative: The objective of the Electricity Transmission and Distribution System Rehabilitation Project for Zambia is to increase the capacity and improve the reliability of the electricity transmission and distribution system in the Lusaka area. The project will reinforce and upgrade the power transmission and distribution infrastructure in Lusaka area as a priority to increase the capacity and improve the reliability of the electricity network for consumers throughout the area. This will improve the quality of electricity supply to existing consumers and facilitate the connection of new customers. The project consists of the following three components: (i) rehabilitation of the 132kV and 88kV transmission network in Lusaka Area; (ii) rehabilitation of the 33kV and 11kV distribution network in Lusaka Area; and (iii) technical assistance and project supervision.
The objectives of the Project are to increase the capacity and improve the reliability of the electricity transmission system in the Lusaka area.

title.narrative: Transmission line segment upgraded in Lusaka West - Coventry

comment.narrative: <p>This activity was segmented into two portions comprising the 6 km of 132kV line from Lusaka West 330/132/33kV Substation to the newly constructed Industrial 132/33/11kV Substation, and the 4 km from Industrial Substation to Coventry Street 132/33/11kV Substation. The first segment involved the task of decommissioning the existing 132kV (1x100 MVA Wolf conductor) single circuit line followed by the construction of a new 132kV (2x200 MVA Kingbird conductor) double circuit line up to Industrial substation, within the samewayleave.  The second segment involved the repairing of the existing lattice towers and restringing of the conductor (from Wolf – 100MVA to High Tension Low Sag, HTLS – 200MVA) between the new industrial substation and Coventry Street substation.The works were finally completed and both lines of the first segment were commissioned on 19 January 2022 and 20 January 2022, while for the second segment between Industrial and Coventry was commissioned on 17 January 2022.</p>
<p>This is estimated based on the current number of household connections in the Lusaka area assuming an average household size of 6.</p>

title.narrative: Transmission line segment upgraded in Waterworks - Lusaka South MFEZ

comment.narrative: <p>This target was to construct a new 20km 132kV 1X180MVA kingbird conductor line from LSMFEZ 330/132/33kV to Water Works 132/33/11kV Substation. This project was part of the original project which had three tasks (LSMFEZ-Water Works, Leopards Hill – Roma and Lusaka West- Coventry via Industrial Substation) which was for thirty-one months, from 02 January 2018 to 31 December 2021. Underthis project, the target was to construct and install new 132kV 1 X 180MVA line from LSMFEZ to Water Works 132/33/11kV Substation. The implementation schedule was affected due to the transposing of the LSMFEZ to Water Works with the Leopards Hill – Water Works line.  However, the works were finally completed and the line was commissioned in April 2021.</p>

<p>A total of 224 people (PIU and other ZESCO staff) were trained against the planned 150.  The staff were trained in various courses with main focus on procurement, financial management, engineering designs and project management.</p>

title.narrative: Transmission line segment upgraded in Leopards Hill -Roma

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Fully achieved.</strong> Activities under this indicator included the decommissioning of the existing 132kV (1x100MVA Wolf conductor) single circuit line, followed by the construction of a new 132kV (2x200MVA Kingbird conductor) double circuit line within the same wayleave. A total of 25 km of line was constructed and commissioned at project completion. Additional benefit was realized with the use of steel monopole structures as they are less prone to vandalism, in comparison to lattice structures.</p>

title.narrative: Transmission lines constructed or rehabilitated under the project

comment.narrative: <p>The target was to upgrade the existing operational 88/33/11kV, 165MVA Waterworks substation (105MVA at the time the power systemstudy was carried out) to 132/33/11kV, 270MVA substation.  The target was to increase capacity with firm supply of 90MVA at 33kV and 60MVA at 11kV. The first phase was the line turning works which were sucessfully completed in August 2019, followed by the commissioning of one 90MVA, 132/33kV Transformer T1 and 2x30MVA 132/11kV Transformers. The load transfers for the 11kV were completed in June 2020 and 33kV loads in September 2020. The second phase involed the relocation of 132/33kV Transformer T2 from old Water Works 88/33/11kV Substation, and its installation and commissioning at the new Water Works 132/33/11kV Substation, together with 1x30MVA, 132/11kV Transformer T3 in December 2020. This contract took long due to the challenges in securing outages. Waterworks substation supplies sensitive circuits and could not be shut down easily.</p>

title.narrative: Transmission capacity along the Lusaka transmission ring

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Under IDA funding, </strong>achieved transmission capacity along the Lusaka transmission ring increased by 227 percent, reaching 1,022MVA against a baseline of 450MVA, and a target of 900MVA. The Lusaka transmission ring comprised of 132kV single circuit lines, namely: Leopards-Roma, Lusaka West-Roma, and the Lusaka West -Coventry lines. After completion of the project, all three mentioned lines were upgraded from a 1x100MVA single circuit (Wolf conductor) for each, to 2x200MVA double circuit for each (using Kingbird conductor), which has higher carrying capacity.  This has created redundancy on the Lusaka transmission ring and improved reliability of supply. Moreover, additional benefit was realized with the use of steel monopole structures as they are less prone to vandalism, in comparison to lattice structures.</p>

title.narrative: Studies completed for preparation of new infrastructure energy projects

comment.narrative: <p> This target was achieved as planned.  The Consultant on the project in conjunction with ZESCO Engineers carried out anetwork study to analyze the integration of the LTDRP Project into the existing Lusaka Distribution Network in selected peri-urban high-density, low-income townships of Lusaka. This study is an input to the design of the integrated Lusaka distribution network under the Last Mile project being funded by the European Union.  Under the funding, about 63,000 households are expected to be connected (at a subsidized connection fee).</p>

title.narrative: Transmission line segment upgraded in Roma -Lusaka West

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Fully achieved</strong>. Activities under this indicator involved the task of decommissioning the existing 132kV (1x100 MVA Wolf conductor) single circuit line followed by the construction of a new 132kV (2x200 MVA Kingbird conductor) double circuit line, within the same wayleave.  The works were finally completed and both lines on 20 km were commissioned on 26 January 2021</p>

title.narrative: Unserved load on the Lusaka transmission network

comment.narrative: <p>The determination of the unserved load was based on the network interruptions experienced on the (old) 132kV Lusaka ring, largely due to the fact that it had exceeded its thermal limit of 470A. The unserved load baseline was captured as 14%. Now thatthe new 132kV ring has been upgraded to 710A (minimum for single circuit) and 1420A (for double circuit corridor). This entails that there are no more interruptions attributed to the lines’ thermal limit.</p>
